CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative evaluation prior to planned right knee replacement surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Nicole Miller is a 76-year-old female with chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction presenting for follow-up. She had an exacerbation of CHF in the spring with increasing dyspnea. BNP was elevated at 3,000 in March and increased to 6,000 in April. Her furosemide was changed to torsemide 20 mg daily and her lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily in March. She reports significant symptomatic improvement since these medication adjustments. She has lost approximately 3-3.5 pounds since last visit in April and notes improved urinary urgency. She denies current dyspnea. She experienced leg cramps in both legs a few days ago, which resolved with pickle juice; she attributes this to sleeping with ceiling fan on. She denies chest pain or palpitations. She had heartburn that worsened in January; she started and then discontinued prilosec after two weeks and has had no recurrence since. She reports normal urinary output and is tolerating medications well. She is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24 and wants to optimize her cardiac status prior to surgery.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current dyspnea, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. Leg cramps resolved. Heartburn resolved. Urinary output normal. Denies fever, chills, or other constitutional symptoms.

- Anemia (history of)

- Right knee osteoarthritis (planned replacement)

2. Pre-operative evaluation for right knee replacement (June 24)
